# MCP for Adobe Premiere Pro

Free, MIT-licensed, local-first Model Context Protocol server for supported Adobe Premiere Pro workflows. Independent of Adobe. Premiere and the selected AI client have their own requirements and costs.

Preferred product name: **MCP for Adobe Premiere Pro**. Common shorthand: Premiere Pro MCP. npm package: premiere-pro-mcp.

## Published package

Current project release: 1.14.8.
Published v1.14.8: 332 core tools, 330 default-profile tools, and 91 authenticated capability-gated UXP additions (421 connected tools).
These counts were checked against the downloaded npm artifact and its matching tag. They do not prove a successful operation in a licensed Premiere host.
Release: https://github.com/leancoderkavy/premiere-pro-mcp/releases/tag/v1.14.8

## Development source, separate from publication

Current source metadata registers 349 core structured MCP tools, 347 in the default profile, and 93 capability-gated tools for 440 connected tools. Source package version: 1.14.8. Main may include changes not in the published package even when its version string is unchanged.

## Start a workflow

Use https://premiere-pro-mcp.com/workflows/ for three downloadable evaluation recipes and synthetic media. The kit is not a recorded live demo or a host-verified project. Project check is read-only; review frames write approved image files; product-spot starter ends at preview.

Install the Claude Desktop bundle and the separate Premiere connector through https://premiere-pro-mcp.com/#install. Other clients use the documented local stdio route. Keep the assistant, server, connector, and Premiere on the same computer for the recommended setup.
First prompt: Safely check my Premiere connection with verify_premiere_connection. Make no changes.
The hosted endpoint does not automatically pair a visitor to their local Premiere. AI client data handling still applies; local-first is not a universal no-upload guarantee.

## Compatibility and limitations

Current release: 1.14.8. Targets Premiere Pro 2020–2026 through CEP on Windows and macOS; UXP needs compatible 25.6.0+ hosts and advertised capabilities. Node.js 20.19+ is required for npm setup; the Claude bundle contains its server runtime.
Editorial context and planning tools do not themselves transcribe media, invoke an LLM, or apply edits. A preview is not an applied operation. A ready connection is not a completed edit. Playback and rendered output require separate inspection.

## Evaluation recipes

### Check a sequence before handoff

Inspect timeline structure, gaps, disabled clips, muted tracks, and offline-source evidence without changing the edit.
Output: A sequence review report for you to compare with Premiere.
Read-only in Premiere. The report does not establish visual quality, rights, caption correctness, or delivery approval.
Availability: Tools documented in v1.14.8. This kit has not been verified inside Premiere.
Tools: verify_premiere_connection, inspect_sequence_review_report
Prompt: Run verify_premiere_connection and stop if it is not ready. On my active disposable test sequence, run inspect_sequence_review_report with default privacy settings. Summarize its findings and limitations. Do not include marker comments or change Premiere.
Recipe: https://premiere-pro-mcp.com/workflows/#project-check
Guide: https://premiere-pro-mcp.com/blog/premiere-pro-ai-workflow-checklist/

### Export a small visual review pack

Ask for a few evenly spaced frames from a bounded sequence range, then compare the files with your timeline.
Output: A small set of image files for your own review.
Writes image files to an approved output folder. It does not change the timeline or prove playback and audio quality.
Availability: Tools documented in v1.14.8. File-export and host verification remain pending.
Tools: verify_premiere_connection, export_sequence_review_frames
Prompt: Run verify_premiere_connection and stop if it is not ready. Help me prepare export_sequence_review_frames for four evenly spaced frames from my disposable active sequence. Ask me for the sequence range and an approved local output folder first. Show the arguments and wait for my confirmation before writing files. Do not upload images or change Premiere.
Recipe: https://premiere-pro-mcp.com/workflows/#review-frames
Guide: https://premiere-pro-mcp.com/blog/premiere-pro-review-frames-and-scene-detection/

### Preview a product-spot assembly

Use existing project items to prepare a short assembly and inspect its targets before deciding whether to apply it.
Output: A proposed assembly for an explicitly chosen disposable sequence.
The starter prompt requests preview only. Application, playback, and final export are separate steps with their own checks.
Availability: Preview tool documented in v1.14.8. No completed product-ad or host-tested assembly is claimed.
Tools: verify_premiere_connection, preview_product_spot
Prompt: Run verify_premiere_connection and stop if it is not ready. Help me prepare preview_product_spot using the two imported kit clips and a disposable sequence with empty target tracks. Inspect the current tool schema and ask me for missing inputs. Show only the preview and affected targets. Do not apply, render, upload, or export anything.
Recipe: https://premiere-pro-mcp.com/workflows/#product-spot
Guide: https://premiere-pro-mcp.com/blog/premiere-pro-workflow-automation/

## Privacy and reporting

The kit uses synthetic media. Do not submit client projects, paths, prompts, transcripts, or tokens in public reports. Optional browser campaign events and local runtime events have no shared editor identifier. Downloads do not establish activation.
Privacy: https://premiere-pro-mcp.com/privacy/
Security: https://github.com/leancoderkavy/premiere-pro-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
